data.body:
LIVE MULTI-TURN AGENTIC MEASUREMENT — the two criteria that were genuinely owed are now met, with
before/after numbers I verified myself from the raw capture files rather than accepting a summary.

WHY A PURPOSE-BUILT HARNESS AND NOT A GATE RUN: I first tried to measure through `rebar review-plan`
four separate ways. Its Pass-1 `finders` step is the only agentic multi-turn step, and it executed in
exactly ONE run out of many; every other run recorded only prerequisite_verify/verify/coach_notes, so
the agentic path was never exercised. Two of those attempts also produced a CONFOUNDED result worth
recording so nobody repeats it: the post-fix arm read exactly the 4,090 tokens the pre-fix arm had
WRITTEN two minutes earlier, inside the 5-minute TTL — i.e. it was reading the other arms entry, not
demonstrating its own mechanism. A paired re-run showed all four arms reading the identical 4,090, which
proved the confound rather than the fix. Those attempts are DISCARDED and cited here only as method.

THE HARNESS: real PydanticAIRunner(cfg).run(RunRequest(..., execution_mode="agentic")) against the live
Anthropic API on anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6. No MockTransport. Per-HTTP-call usage captured at the
`_wrapped_transport` seam of `anthropic_model._build_retrying_anthropic_model`, delegating to a real
httpx transport. Two guards, both load-bearing: an ARM GUARD that aborts unless the live
`cache_settings_for()` output matches the intended arm, and a per-sequence nonce in the system prompt so
no stale entry from an earlier run can be read.

THE ARMS WERE GENUINELY DIFFERENT — confirmed from the recorded live settings, not assumed:
  B (pre-dd27): {anthropic_cache_instructions, anthropic_cache_tool_definitions}
  A (post-dd27): the same PLUS anthropic_cache: True     <- the third breakpoint

THE WORKLOAD WAS IDENTICAL — request_bytes per call:
  B2: 4981, 15930, 26776, 37624, 48470, 59315, 70163, 81008, 91854
  A2: 5029, 15978, 26824, 37672, 48518, 59363, 70211, 81056, 91902
  A difference of EXACTLY 48 bytes at every step — the `cache_control` directive itself. Same work.
MULTI-TURN WAS ACHIEVED, COUNTED NOT ASSUMED: tool_results_in_request = 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 across the 9
LLM calls, i.e. 9 calls / 8 tool-using turns, history growing by one ~2,594-token tool result per turn.

B2 vs A2 (each arms SECOND run, so both compare against a warm cache written by their own arm):
                        B2 (pre-dd27)     A2 (post-dd27)
  LLM calls / tool turns      9 / 8            9 / 8
  total prompt tokens       109,029          109,029
  cache_read                 11,160           88,244
  cache_write                     0           20,775
  UNCACHED input             97,869               10

THE ATTRIBUTION IS THE PER-CALL SHAPE, not a difference of totals — this is the part that answers the
criterion "attributable to the message tail rather than only to the system block":
  B2 cache_read is FLAT 1,240 on every one of the 9 calls, INDEPENDENT of how much history the request
    carries. 1,240 is the system-prompt + tool-definitions prefix — exactly the two pre-existing
    breakpoints. Meanwhile uncached input climbs 480 -> 3,093 -> 5,688 -> ... -> 21,254: the accumulated
    tool-result history re-billed at full price every turn. THAT IS THE O(N^2) SHAPE, MEASURED.
  A2 cache_read GROWS MONOTONICALLY 1,718 -> 4,332 -> 6,927 -> ... -> 19,899, in steps of ~2,594 — one
    step per tool result added. The growing part IS the message tail; nothing else in the request grows.
  Tail-attributable cache_read = 88,244 - 11,160 = 77,084 tokens (7.9x more cache reads).
  A third fully-warm arm-A run: 109,019 of 109,029 prompt tokens served from cache = 99.99%.

DERIVED COST (arithmetic from published sonnet rates, NOT a measured invoice — stated as derived):
  at $3.00/$0.30/$3.75 per MTok for input/cache-read/cache-write: B2 ~ $0.297, A2 ~ $0.104, warm ~ $0.033
  => ~2.8x cheaper on the first warm run, ~9x at steady state, for byte-identical work.

VERIFIED BY ME, not taken from the agents summary: I re-read B2/A2/A3.percall.json and independently
recomputed every figure above — the flat 1,240 column, the monotonic growth, the 11,160 / 88,244 /
109,019 totals, the 97,869 -> 10 uncached collapse, the 0..8 tool-result progression and the 48-byte
request delta. All match.

DISCLOSURE OF AN ERROR OF MINE THAT AFFECTED THIS EXPERIMENT: I committed in the same worktree while the
harness was mid-run, which transiently reverted the arm-B patch and invalidated its first two runs. They
were discarded and the arm guard was added precisely because of it. The five reported runs all passed
that guard. Evidence files: /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-evidence-dd27/{B1,B2,A1,A2,A3}.percall.json and the
matching *.usage.jsonl (note rebar writes ONE usage row per run() aggregating all 9 HTTP calls, with
"requests": 9 — the per-HTTP detail is in the percall files).
